t: You're on Addison Avenue, a broad, tree-lined street in Notting Hill, in the wealthy Holland Park area. It runs north from Holland Park Avenue up to St James's Gardens and St James's Church, and it is largely residential. The street takes its name from Joseph Addison, the essayist, poet and politician. He founded The Spectator magazine with his friend Richard Steele, and his plain prose style helped end the mannered habits of the seventeenth century. He also wrote the play Cato, a Tragedy, in 1712.
